A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same DetGain study. Their complete main texts, figures, tables, equations, and appendices support comparison, including matching retained material across renumbering and relocation.

before.justification: v1 reports original COCO detection experiments, noise and pseudo-label evaluations, ablations, and Monte Carlo simulations.

after.justification: v2 retains those original results and adds VOC and BDD100K evaluations, ranking and additivity simulations, and computational analyses.

M1.justification: Appendix 8 adds a dynamic sampling policy: retain 40% of candidates for the first 60% of iterations, then 20% for the remainder. v1 evaluates fixed ratios. The core teacher–student DetGain scoring, augmentation pipeline, and Algorithm 1 remain unchanged; polynomial approximation was already described in v1.

E1.justification: v1 evaluates COCO, including corrupted annotations and additional pseudo-labeled COCO images. v2 Appendix 7 adds Pascal VOC2007/2012 and BDD100K, with evaluation on VOC2007 test and BDD100K validation. This substantially broadens coverage to smaller generic-detection data and a driving domain.

E2.justification: The sampling comparators in v1 Table 5 and v2 Table 4 are unchanged: uniform sampling, GradNorm, hard mining, classification entropy, entropy/information/diversity, Image-AP, and loss-learnability. PKD and CrossKD comparisons also remain unchanged. The additional benchmarks compare DetGain with the same baseline strategy.

E3.justification: v2 adds prior-ranking simulations using 64-image batches and 100 predictions per image, batch-additivity tests varying base-set size, a 0.5×–3× FCOS schedule sweep, and dynamic-versus-fixed sampling evaluation. Appendix 7 specifies splits, ResNet-50, 1× schedules, and COCO-style mAP for the additional datasets. The earlier fixed-batch sampling-ratio sweep is removed; principal COCO training recipes remain unchanged.

E4.justification: New analyses test uniform-versus-fitted-prior ranking agreement (Figure 4), additive batch-score accuracy and ranking stability (Figure 6), runtime and memory costs, longer training, and dynamic sampling (Appendix 8). Conversely, v1 Table 4's sampling-ratio sensitivity study is removed. Earlier noise, teacher, pseudo-label, prior-performance, and Monte Carlo analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Table 1 newly reports means and standard deviations over three different seeds across the six detectors; v1 provides point estimates without a run count. New Figure 4 includes a 95% confidence band, and Figure 6 reports mean±standard deviation. Additional-dataset results explicitly use single runs. The PDFs establish expanded reporting, not an increase from a known v1 run count.

E6.justification: New results include VOC mAP 51.3 versus 54.3 and BDD100K 30.3 versus 32.1 (Table 11), prior-ranking correlation around 0.94, and FCOS 3× results of 37.1 versus 43.8 (Table 13). Dynamic sampling reports 42.5 versus static sampling's 43.0 mAP with approximately 30% less training time. Table 1 replaces point estimates with three-run summaries, including ATSS DetGain AP 41.6→41.5 and FCOS 40.9→41.0. Earlier sampling-ratio results disappear; retained sampler and KD comparison tables keep their values.

T1.justification: The AP definitions, single-insertion derivations, and uniform-prior closed forms remain unchanged. v2 Eq. (27) numbers the same first-order additivity expression already present in v1. New simulations provide empirical support rather than a new proof; polynomial formulas elaborate the previously described approximation.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the central claims of model-agnostic, AP-aligned online curation, complementarity with augmentation and distillation, and robustness to noisy labels. Added experiments strengthen support without redefining the main contribution or novelty claim.

C2.justification: Appendix 3 adds explanations involving cancellation of approximation bias in teacher–student differences and post-NMS handling of within-image interactions. Appendix 8 interprets longer-schedule results as evidence of reduced overfitting rather than merely extra computation. Section 4.5 removes the assertion that joint KD and curation share one teacher pass without additional computational cost.

D1.justification: Appendix 8 expands polynomial-weight implementation details, including optional class weights, post-NMS top-K predictions, and highest-score TP deduplication, and reports timing and memory measurements. The Python-style Listing 1 is removed, but Algorithm 1 and detailed augmentation settings remain. These are limited documentation changes around the retained implementation.

R1.justification: v2 adds the Pascal VOC and BDD100K references and removes the TeachAugment reference associated with shortened future-work discussion. Positioning relative to online curation, active learning, coreset selection, and knowledge distillation remains unchanged.

P1.justification: Revisions are localized to the ablation discussion, expanded Appendix 3 explanations, shortened KD and conclusion passages, and new Appendices 7–8. The title, abstract, introduction, related work, and main method narrative are substantially unchanged. The Python listing is removed and appendix headings receive minor editing.

P2.justification: v2 adds ranking and additivity plots and tables for additional datasets, runtime, and training schedules, while removing the earlier sampling-ratio table. Table 1 drops the Learning Proxy column and incorporates uncertainty values. Several retained figures, tables, and Algorithm 1 move, producing substantial changes to experimental displays despite retaining the two-column style.

improvement.justification: v2 substantially strengthens empirical credibility: three-seed reporting addresses uncertainty in the main results, additional datasets test applicability beyond COCO, and ranking/additivity checks directly examine central approximations. Runtime breakdowns and longer-training controls also improve assessment of practical value. Removing the sampling-ratio ablation weakens support for the default ratio, and the new benchmarks remain single-run, but these drawbacks do not outweigh the stronger validation of the paper's central claims.
